close_reason: false positive: the distinction is intentional and documented — producedAt future means tampered/malformed response (OcspMalformed), thisUpdate future means SingleResponse not yet valid (OcspExpired per consistent caller semantics); both doc comments explain the rationale
description: In ocsp.rs check_revocation, line 176: if now < producedAt → OcspMalformed. But line 183: if now < thisUpdate → OcspExpired. Both cases mean 'the OCSP data is invalid at this point in time' but they use different error codes. The comment at line 180 explains producedAt is 'structurally suspicious' while thisUpdate is the same 'freshness failure as a past-due nextUpdate'. This asymmetry means callers cannot handle 'OCSP not yet valid' consistently — they must check two error variants. A consistent error code (or a unified OcspNotYetValid variant) would simplify callers. P3 quality issue.
title: OCSP: producedAt future check returns OcspMalformed but thisUpdate future check returns OcspExpired — inconsistent error semantics
